title: A difficult day
paragraphs: My name is Ainur Ospanova. I am twenty years old and I am from Kostanay. I am a second-year Medicine student at WKU. Yesterday was Monday, the twelfth of October, and it was, without any doubt, one of the most difficult days of my life at university. I am going to tell you honestly about everything that went wrong.

The morning was a disaster from the very beginning. My alarm clock was broken — it was silent all night. I woke up late and I was in a panic. Breakfast was impossible. By the time I ran to the cafeteria, it was already full of students and the queue was very long. I only had time for a glass of water. Outside, the weather was cold and grey. There was a strong wind and it was raining. My umbrella was at home in Kostanay. I was wet, cold, and hungry before my first lecture even started.

My first lecture was on Human Anatomy — one of the most important subjects in Medicine. I was almost ten minutes late when I arrived. The door was heavy and it made a loud noise when I opened it. All fifty students turned to look at me. The professor, Dr. Seitkali, was not happy. Her expression was stern and she was silent for a moment before she continued. I was so embarrassed. My face was red for the next twenty minutes.

The second lecture was even worse. There was an unexpected written quiz on the material from the previous week. I was completely unprepared — I was sure the quiz was scheduled for Friday, not Monday. The questions were very difficult. My mind was blank. The results were disappointing: I was in the bottom third of the group. It was a painful moment.

At lunchtime, I was exhausted and hungry. The cafeteria was crowded — every table was full. The queue was long and slow. When I finally reached the counter, the chicken soup was already cold and there was no bread left. I was alone because my friends were at a different lecture and were not free for lunch. The cafeteria was noisy and I was miserable. It was the loneliest hour of my week.

In the afternoon, I was in the library for three hours. The internet connection was slow and my laptop was almost out of battery. My notes from Monday's anatomy lecture were incomplete because I was late. I was frustrated and tired. But I was also determined. I found the textbook on the shelf and I was at my desk for the whole afternoon, filling in the gaps in my notes. The library was warm, at least, and that was something.

By the evening, my head was full of new information and my body was completely exhausted. I was back in my dormitory room by eight o'clock. My roommate Gulnara was there — she was kind and caring. She made a big cup of tea for both of us and we were sitting together in silence for a while. That moment of quiet companionship was the best part of the entire day. It was exactly what I needed.

Yesterday was terrible. But today is a new day. Medicine is the hardest subject at WKU — everyone knows that. The road is long and the days are sometimes very hard. But I was always certain of one thing: I want to be a doctor. That dream was strong yesterday, and it is even stronger today.

dialogue.speaker: Gulnara
dialogue.text: Ainur, you look exhausted. Was yesterday difficult?

dialogue.speaker: Ainur
dialogue.text: It was a complete disaster, Gulnara. From start to finish.

dialogue.speaker: Gulnara
dialogue.text: Oh no! Were you late for your lecture?

dialogue.speaker: Ainur
dialogue.text: Almost ten minutes late! My alarm was broken. I was so embarrassed.

dialogue.speaker: Ainur
dialogue.text: She was not happy. Her face was very stern. It was awful.

dialogue.speaker: Gulnara
dialogue.text: Was there a quiz? You mentioned something about a quiz.

dialogue.speaker: Ainur
dialogue.text: Yes! It was unexpected. I was totally unprepared. The questions were so hard.

dialogue.speaker: Gulnara
dialogue.text: Were your friends with you at lunch?

dialogue.speaker: Ainur
dialogue.text: No — they were at a different lecture. I was completely alone.

dialogue.speaker: Ainur
dialogue.text: It was packed! The soup was cold and there was no bread left.

dialogue.speaker: Gulnara
dialogue.text: You were so brave to keep going. Were you in the library after?

dialogue.speaker: Ainur
dialogue.text: Yes, for three hours. I was tired but I was determined. Like always.
